items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-03

ctx.x: Well, I found that Max Kaminsky worked out very well with Sidney. And at that time, most of the people that wanted to hear Sidney were really interested in hearing him play Summertime on the fish horn. And we're not very discriminating about bands anyway. It seemed like I was the only one who was worried about the sound of the band. But frequently, and maybe usually, when I hired Sidney for a job, I'd also hire a clarinet player who played mainly the ensemble parts. And it was not uncommon for me to have both…
That worked certainly. Let's see. We were talking about recording sessions. It was Joe Maera- Mm-hm. He worked with him. Were you working for Joe Maera- Mm-hm.

Not really. What was the basis? No. Let me see what would I say was the basis. Joe, as you know, was very much interested in getting the music of New Orleans recorded. recorded. He has a feeling of commitment about it, the fact that there are a lot of musicians who hadn't been recorded or hadn't been recorded properly. And of course I felt the same way about it, and I always thought of myself as helping out, you know, in many cases proposing and producing sessions myself that I thought were suitable. And so there…
